answerClaimProvenance.text: The paper reviews the state of the art on conversational systems from three perspectives: types of interactions, types of architecture, and types of context reasoning, and consolidates them in a comparison table.
In the reviewed state of the art, most proposed approaches for context reasoning rely on rules using logics and knowledge bases.
The most recent state of the art for developing such systems has employed Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Dynamic Context-Sensitive Generation, and Memory Networks, among others.
Sukhbaatar's work presents the state of the art of recent efforts to capture dialogue context as long-term structure within sequences using RNNs or LSTM-based models.

Among the reviewed systems, ELIZA was one of the first software programs created to understand natural language processing, built by Joseph Weizenbaum at MIT in 1966 and known for acting like a psychotherapist.

ELIZA was created to tackle five fundamental technical problems: identifying critical words, discovering a minimal context, choosing appropriate transformations, generating appropriate responses, and providing an ending capacity for ELIZA scripts.
PARRY was developed by Kenneth Colby, a psychiatrist at Stanford University, in the early 1970s.
A.L.I.C.E. appeared in 1995, and its current version uses AIML, an XML language designed for creating stimulus-response chat robots.
Cleverbot (1997-2014) is a chatbot developed by the British AI scientist Rollo Carpenter.
The paper states that most existing chatbots, from ELIZA to modern state-of-the-art ones, fall into this category.

The paper notes a lack of methods and tools to design and engineer coordination and mediation among chatbots and humans, and a lack of research on building coordination laws integrated with natural language for chatbot engines.

The authors state that, to the best of their knowledge, the architecture proposed in the paper is the first in the state of the art designed to support coordinated aware chatbots in a multiparty conversation.
